correctness.rationale: Angular orthogonality and polar integration give the complete monomial basis with M_n=(2π/α)2^(−(2n+2)/α)Γ((2n+2)/α). Integration sends e_n to j/(n+j)·sqrt(M_(n+j)/M_n)e_(n+j) for z^j. The gamma-ratio exponent is j/α−1 and the constant is jα^(−j/α); orthogonal output degrees prevent cancellation in the unbounded case, and vanishing fixed-step weights give compactness. A nonzero Taylor leading term always goes up in degree, so no nonzero eigenvalue exists. In the critical case d=α the difference from a_d S^d is compact: the shift's index inside the disk is −d by splitting into the d one-step shifts, and outside the disk index zero plus injectivity gives invertibility. Closedness handles the boundary. The disk and equation (1) concern that critical case, as in the proof; reading the disk assertion for an arbitrary subcritical degree would contradict the compact case. For the two-column test with separation d−q, the overlap (d,q) is unique at its leading order n^(q/d−1) and has the stated absolute coefficient; all other overlaps decay faster. The two diagonal defects are O(n^−1)+O(n^(2q/d−2)), both little-o of the overlap. A unit-phase equal-weight superposition therefore gives exactly the positive defect claimed. In the pure critical case Γ(x+2)/Γ(x)=x(x+1) gives (3); per residue, the product of the two beta variables has nth moment equal to the product of squared weights. Haar angle times that radial law gives a bounded multiplication normal extension. Subnormality implies hyponormality by compression, and for hyponormal operators log-convexity of ||T^n v|| yields ||T^n||≥||T||^n, hence normaloidity. Compact nonzero cases have r=0 and fail. An independent 70-digit check at (d,q)=(3,1),(5,3),(8,7) with complex coefficients reconstructed the phase-aligned vector and obtained witness-to-leading-term ratios 0.9999999772, 1.0000000000, 1.001794173 at n=10^24 (review_checks/volterra.py); these spot checks are not the classification proof.

evidence: The existing spectral formula is invariant under the lower degree perturbation. The monomial result supplies a normal extension for a single degree; the Gaussian result restricts to degree at most two on the classical space.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither compactness of the perturbation nor the pure subnormal case fixes the perturbed norm. The phase-aligned overlap controlling all higher critical orders is a material additional result; no priority claim is made for the spectrum or the pure case.
